UTA.head: The Mammoth start a half-step ahead
UTA.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Even though Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Colorado may be without Makar. Still, it’s close: the Avalanche can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Mammoth are searching for answers
paras: The Mammoth are winless in four (0-2-2), and the Avalanche (11-6-3) lost 4-3 in overtime to Ottawa on Thursday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avs third (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Mammoth fifth (tied for 14th).

The Avalanche’s record (.625) is about what their chances are worth. The Mammoth have played better than their record (.550) says: their chances are worth about .697, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Avalanche get their defensemen shooting (1st) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest), so the Mammoth get in close, but them mostly shoot from distance. Colorado has scored 4.05 goals a game, the second most in the league. On the other side, the Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (3rd). Something has to give when the Avalanche’s shooting runs into the Mammoth’s defense.

Martin Nečas (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (14 G / 5 A / 19 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, fifth in the NHL. For the Mammoth, Clayton Keller (5 G / 20 A / 25 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mikhail Sergachev (5 G / 15 A / 20 P in 20 GP) is next in line.

Mackenzie Blackwood (10-3-1 / .901 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Colorado. Utah has two options in net: Karel Vejmelka (6-6-1 / .876 SV% in 13 GS) and Sebastian Cossa (4-2-1 / .864 SV% in 7 GS). Vejmelka has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Avalanche are newly without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.

The Mammoth are newly without Nate Schmidt, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche are missing more right now.
Anders Lee has four goals in six games against Colorado since 2023-24, most of them with the Islanders.
Artturi Lehkonen has 14 goals on chances worth about 7.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
